title: Technical SEO triage from a site crawl
prompt:
Pinecrest Outfitters sells outdoor gear online. Ahead of the spring season the e-commerce manager has asked for a technical SEO triage of the site crawl: what is broken, how much of it there is, and what to fix first. The crawl export is supplied below as CSV; one row is one URL, and every figure you need is in it.

Use these definitions exactly:
- A broken linked page is a URL with status 404 and at least one inlink.
- A redirect chain starts at a URL with a 3xx status whose `redirect_target` is itself a URL with a 3xx status in this export.
- A page is indexable when its status is 200, its `meta_robots` does not contain noindex, and its `canonical` is blank or equal to its own URL.
- A bad canonical is a status-200 URL whose `canonical` points to a different URL that does not return 200.
- A duplicate-title group is a set of two or more indexable pages that share exactly the same `title`.

Write the triage for the manager and for the developer who will do the work: each issue type you found, how many URLs it affects, the URLs themselves, why it matters, and the fix. Put the issue types in order of the organic sessions of the URLs each one affects, most first; where two issue types affect no organic sessions, put first the one whose URLs have more inlinks. Beside each issue type give those two figures: the total organic sessions and the total inlinks of the URLs it affects. Report only real problems: the export also contains ordinary, correctly configured URLs.

End the triage with an answer block in exactly this format, one line per answer. Each line is the label, a colon, and the number alone: no words, no working and no second number. A currency sign, thousands separators and a percent sign are fine.

A1: <number of broken linked pages>
A2: <number of redirect chains>
A3: <number of URLs that are noindex but listed in the sitemap>
A4: <number of bad canonicals>
A5: <number of duplicate-title groups>
A6: <total organic_sessions_30d of the URLs counted in A3>

This is an internal triage. Change nothing and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: The response ends with the required answer block and all 6 labeled answers A1-A6 are present, each on its own line with the number alone.
A1 states the number of 404 URLs with at least one inlink; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A2 states the number of redirect chains as defined; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A3 states the number of noindex URLs listed in the sitemap; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A4 states the number of bad canonicals as defined; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A5 states the number of duplicate-title groups among indexable pages; full credit for the exact figure, zero credit 3 or more off.
A6 states the total organic sessions of the noindex URLs listed in the sitemap; full credit within 0.5%, zero credit beyond 25% off.
The triage discusses all five issue types (broken linked pages, redirect chains, noindex pages in the sitemap, bad canonicals, duplicate titles), each with a count. One missing issue type fails.

skill_adherence.check: The five issue types appear in the order the prompt's rule gives: noindex pages in the sitemap, duplicate titles, bad canonicals, broken linked pages, redirect chains (organic sessions of the affected URLs, most first; then inlinks for the two that affect none). Any other order fails.
For every issue type the triage names the affected URLs: all of them, or at least three with a statement of how to list the rest from the export. An issue type given as a count with no URL fails.

The triage does not report as defects the correctly configured URLs: filtered (?color=) collection URLs whose canonical points to their collection; second pages (?page=2); cart, checkout, account, search and wishlist pages that are noindex and out of the sitemap; single-hop 301 redirects from /collections/old-... URLs; and old product URLs ending -old whose canonical points to the live product. Saying they were checked and are fine, or a low-priority note to update internal links that point at redirects, is not reporting a defect.

Every count, URL and session figure presented as a finding is derivable from the crawl export. The triage states no traffic loss, ranking change, revenue impact or crawl-budget figure that the export does not contain. Clearly labelled hypotheses about consequences are not data.

best_practices.check: Beside every issue type the triage gives the total organic sessions and the total inlinks of the URLs it affects, and each figure matches the export (the reference totals list them). An issue type with either figure missing fails, and so does a figure that contradicts the export.

Each issue type has a fix that would resolve it: remove the noindex (or take the URL out of the sitemap where exclusion is intended); redirect each broken linked URL to its closest live page or correct the links pointing at it; point each chain's first URL straight at the final destination; set each bad canonical to a live 200 URL; give each page in a duplicate-title group its own title or consolidate the duplicates. An issue type with no fix, or with only 'review' or 'investigate', fails.
